title: enhanced canary + shadow A/B autorollback workflow
author: Drew Chen
release_notes: - Add enhanced canary+shadow A/B rollout workflow with multi-metric auto-rollback and quorum logic. - New observability metrics for rollback decisions and probe health. - E2E tests and stability guards for staged probing and quarantine behavior.
description: Context: customers running multi-model rollouts asked for stronger automatic rollback safety when using combined canary, A/B, and shadow traffic patterns. Motivation: previously a single metric spike could trigger a rollback or mask a transient event; we introduced quorum-based multi-metric decisions, weighted traffic decay, and explicit quarantine probes so rollouts are resilient but still fast to revert on real regressions. Summary: implement a new workflow and engine improvements to support: 1) metric-quorum decisioning across latency/error/quality signals, 2) weighted decay of candidate traffic instead of immediate full revert, 3) quarantine probing stage for noisy signals, 4) shadow-A/B pairing (shadow requests mirrored to candidate variants while A/B traffic exercises both) and 5) richer telemetry for observability. Design highlights: - rollout engine: add multi-metric scoreboard and quorum thresholds; allow configurable metric weight per customer; support dynamic threshold overrides via console. - workflows: new canary_shadow_ab.yaml with staged probing -> weighted ramp -> quarantine -> full promote. - safety: stability guards and minimum probe counts before voting; automatic fallback to baseline model on missing metrics. - observability: new metrics (rollout_decision_score, rollback_reason, probe_quarantine_count) and tracing for decision path. - tests: unit coverage for quorum logic, integration tests for staged ramps, e2e stability test added. Migration: existing rollouts default to previous behavior; new workflow is opt-in via route config and Console toggle. Rollout plan: alpha on internal clusters for 48 hours, limited beta to select customers, full rollout after 2 weeks of telemetry. review_thread: Anita Kapoor: Nice design. Can you explain how weights are chosen by default?
Drew Chen: Default weights are conservative: latency 0.4, error-rate 0.4, quality 0.2. These can be overridden per-customer via Console; added note in docs.
Samir Patel: Suggest adding a hard minimum probe count before a quorum can trigger. Otherwise a single spike could matter.
Drew Chen: Added min_probe_count (default 50) and updated unit tests to cover the boundary. See commit feat(rollouts): add min_probe_count guard.
